problem:
The entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & k & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

equals $-1.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(1\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot k)+(0\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot 3)+(0\cdot k-1\cdot 3) \\  & =2(k-2)+3-3 \\  & =2k-4\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{23}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{23}^{t}={c}_{32}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{32} & =(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 0) \\  & =-(-2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23}^{′} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{23}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{32} \\  & =\frac{2}{2k-4} \\  & =\frac{1}{k-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{23}^{′}=-1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{k-2} & =-1 \\ 1 & =-(k-2) \\ k-2 & =-1 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
